name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention (domain=save/screen-block, descriptor=to_buffer). Accurately describes the function: snapshots a live screen region into a backup buffer (writes an 8-byte header then copies pixels). No Ghidra address residue. It is the exact inverse companion of fd2_restore_screen_block_from_buffer, and the name pairing is consistent.
purpose: Outer setter for a 'save under' screen-block snapshot: writes an 8-byte header (width, height, src_offset) into a backup buffer and hands off to fd2_save_block_loop to pack the live region's pixels contiguously, for later restore by fd2_restore_screen_block_from_buffer.
logic_summary: Stores (uint16)width into data_fd2_graphics_rle_blit_cur_width (0x627B4) and into out_buf[+0]; stores (uint16)height into data_fd2_graphics_rle_blit_remaining_rows (0x627B6) and into out_buf[+2]; stores src_offset (the EAX value, NOT src_base) into out_buf[+4]; computes src = src_base + src_offset and dst = out_buf + 8; calls fd2_save_block_loop(src, dst, stride). In the binary header writes are STOSW/STOSW/STOSD so EDI ends at out_buf+8; ESI=src_base is advanced by ADD ESI,EAX(=src_offset); EBP=stride from [EBP+0x1c]. PUSHAD/POPAD wrap the body; plain RET (cdecl, callers ADD ESP,0x18); EAX untouched so the decompiler 'return in_EAX' is a pass-through artifact and the function is effectively void (all 3 callers discard).
signature: void fd2_save_screen_block_to_buffer(uint32 out_buf, uint32 width, uint32 height, uint32 src_base, uint32 src_offset, uint32 stride)

params.name: out_buf
params.semantics: Backup buffer base; receives the 8-byte header (width word 0, height word 2, src_offset dword 4) then the width*height saved pixel bytes at +8.
params.reason: Descriptive and accurate; no address residue. Matches its use as the STOSW/STOSW/STOSD destination cursor.

params.name: width
params.semantics: Columns copied per row; stored as a word in the header (+0) and in the width global data_fd2_graphics_rle_blit_cur_width.

params.name: height
params.semantics: Row count; stored as a word in the header (+2) and in the height global data_fd2_graphics_rle_blit_remaining_rows (read by the inner loop as the row counter).

params.name: src_base
params.semantics: Source base linear address of the live screen region; src = src_base + src_offset gives the region top-left (ESI in the binary).
params.reason: Correctly distinguishes the base from the offset; matches ESI register role and caller usage (dst surface base passed here).

params.name: src_offset
params.semantics: Offset added to src_base to reach the region's top-left; also stored in the header at +4 so the restore companion can re-derive its dst top-left (mirrors restore's dst_offset).
params.reason: Critical to name this an offset (not a pointer); it is the EAX value that STOSD writes to header+4 and that ADD ESI,EAX applies to src_base. Name is precise; no residue.

params.name: stride
params.semantics: Bytes to advance the source per row inside fd2_save_block_loop (EBP in the binary, from [EBP+0x1c]).
params.reason: Accurate per-row advance semantics; no residue.

returns.semantics: No meaningful return. The decompiler shows 'return in_EAX' but PUSHAD/POPAD leave EAX at its entry value; all three callers discard it.

notes: Src comment (blitspr.c lines 1757-1816) was already precise and accurate (correct 6-param cdecl signature, correct src_offset-at-+4 semantics, correct void-return rationale) -> comment kept, src NOT edited. Disassembly verified: STOSD writes EAX=src_offset (param 5) to header+4, then ADD ESI,EAX gives src=src_base+src_offset; matches src exactly. Ghidra plate was updated because it described only 3 stack params with 'remaining via registers' (a decompiler artifact) and labelled header+4 as 'src_ptr (original screen address)' rather than the offset it actually is; plate now aligns with src's accurate 6-param cdecl framing. No logic changed. Since src was not edited, no blitspr.c diff exists for the clobber check; only the shard is staged.
